title: fileNeighbours(): related files from the Graphify graph.json
brief:
TypeScript run directly by Node 24 (imports end in .ts, erasable syntax only, no new packages). Read src/graph.ts and test/pick.ts (test style: node:assert/strict, prints `<name> PASS`).
Graphify's graph.json (networkx node-link) looks like: { nodes: [{ id: "math_add", label: "add()", source_file: "math.js" }], links: [{ source: "test", target: "math_add", relation: "imports", source_file: "test.js" }] }. source_file paths are repo-relative and may use backslashes on Windows.
1. In src/graph.ts add `export function fileNeighbours(graphFile: string, files: string[], max = 25): string[]`. Return [] when the file is missing or unparsable. Map node id -> source_file (normalise \ to /). For each link whose two nodes are in different files where exactly one file is in `files` (exact match, or the entry ends with / and the path starts with it): emit `<fromFile> <relation> <toFile>` (direction as in the link, use source node file -> target node file). Deduplicate, sort, cap at max.
2. Create test/graph.ts: write a small graph.json to a temp dir with 3 files (a.ts imports b.ts, c.ts calls a.ts, one link inside a.ts) and assert fileNeighbours(file, ["a.ts"]) equals ["a.ts imports b.ts", "c.ts calls a.ts"]; a missing file gives []; a folder entry "src/" matches "src/x.ts". Print `graph PASS`.
3. package.json: append ` && node test/graph.ts` to the "test" script.
Do not change buildCodeGraph or any other file.

title: Workers see their files' neighbours from the code map
brief:
TypeScript run directly by Node 24 (imports end in .ts). src/graph.ts now exports `fileNeighbours(graphFile: string, files: string[], max?: number): string[]` (lines like "a.ts imports b.ts"). Read workerPrompt in src/prompts.ts and the agent.delegate node in src/nodes/agent.ts (line ~166 builds the prompt with depReports).
1. In src/prompts.ts add `neighbours: string[]` to workerPrompt's options object and, right after the `otherTasks(s, t)` entry, add: `o.neighbours.length ? `RELATED FILES (from the code map: what your files use and what uses them; read them when your change affects them, edit only ALLOWED FILES):
${o.neighbours.join("
")}` : ""`.
2. In src/nodes/agent.ts import fileNeighbours from "../graph.ts" and pass `neighbours: t.files.length ? fileNeighbours(path.join(engine.cfg.vault, "Code", s.project.name, "graph.json"), t.files) : []` to workerPrompt (import path from node:path if not imported).
Done when checks pass. Change nothing else.

title: tasks workflow refreshes the code map first

checks.name: workflow
checks.cmd: node src/cli.ts workflow tasks | grep -q codemap

brief:
JSON only. Read workflows/default.json (its first node is {"id": "codemap", "type": "context.codemap"} with an edge {"from": "codemap", "to": "understand"}) and workflows/tasks.json ("start": "next").
In workflows/tasks.json: 1. add node {"id": "codemap", "type": "context.codemap", "position": [750, 0]} as the first entry of "nodes"; 2. set "start" to "codemap"; 3. add edge {"from": "codemap", "to": "next"} as the first entry of "edges". Keep the file's 2-space formatting. Change nothing else.
